name: Lenis
one_liner: Free, MIT-licensed lightweight smooth-scroll JavaScript library by darkroom.engineering, with React, Vue, Framer and snap add-ons.
what_it_offers: A small (under 5kb, no dependencies) library that turns native scroll into smooth, lerp-interpolated scrolling in one line (new Lenis()). It uses no CSS transforms and does not hijack the scrollbar, and it keeps WebGL/DOM and GSAP ScrollTrigger in sync. It supports horizontal and vertical scroll, infinite scroll, nested scroll, and snapping via lenis/snap. There are lenis/react and lenis/vue packages and a no-code Framer plugin. The site also has a showcase of sites using it (with a submit form), templates, and docs that link to the GitHub README.
tech_stack: Vanilla TypeScript/JS; adapters for React, Vue, Framer
portfolio_fit_reason: Lenis is the default smooth-scroll layer on award-style creative portfolios. It syncs with GSAP ScrollTrigger and WebGL, and it takes one line to add to a Next.js or Vite portfolio.
client_ok_note: MIT license on the GitHub repo and the npm package, so it's fine for commercial and client sites.
best_use_for_portfolio: Add <ReactLenis root /> to the portfolio layout and hook it to GSAP ScrollTrigger. That gives case-study pages smooth pinned sections, parallax project images and scrubbed reveals. Respect prefers-reduced-motion, and use data-lenis-prevent on scrollable galleries or modals.
tier_reason: The default smooth-scroll layer on scroll-driven creative portfolios. Tiny, one-line setup, and it pairs directly with GSAP ScrollTrigger and WebGL.
score_rationale: Many award-style sites use Lenis for smooth scrolling, and it pairs directly with GSAP ScrollTrigger and WebGL. It is a narrow utility rather than a design source, but it is key to that premium scroll feel and easy for a coding agent to wire into Next.js or Vite.
free_tier: Everything is free: the core library, the React/Vue/snap packages, and the Framer plugin. The project is funded by GitHub Sponsors and darkroom client work.
commercial_use_license: MIT license (GitHub repo and npm), so commercial use is allowed.
agent_friendly: npm package 'lenis' (plus lenis/react, lenis/vue, lenis/snap). lenis.dev/llms.txt gives a codebase overview and the options. The README has clear copy-paste setup, including GSAP ScrollTrigger sync. No MCP server or shadcn registry found.
maintenance_signal: GitHub darkroomengineering/lenis: about 15.8k stars, last push 2026-09-09. npm latest is 1.3.26 (2026-08-05), with 2.0.0-dev.3 on the dev tag. About 1.1M npm downloads a week (2026-09-05 to 09-11).
caveats: Overdone smooth scroll can hurt usability and accessibility (reduced-motion users, scroll-position expectations). Limits listed in the README: no CSS scroll-snap support (use lenis/snap), capped at 60fps on Safari (30fps in low-power mode), no smooth scroll over iframes, position: fixed can lag on pre-M1 macOS Safari, and nested scroll containers need configuration (allowNestedScroll or data-lenis-prevent). It is a scroll engine only, with no animations or components. A 2.0 rewrite is in dev, so the API may change.
